title: Tensor computation from a specified bounded-above finite free sheaf resolution
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $K^i=0$ for $i>b$ for some integer $b$, and supply isomorphisms $\theta_i:K^i\xrightarrow{\sim}B^{r_i}$ with each $r_i$ a finite nonnegative integer and $r_i=0$ for $i>b$. Then every $K^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $K^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Suppose $M$ is a $B$-module sheaf and $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to M[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every $B$-module sheaf $N$, there is an isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$M[0]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N[0]\cong Q(T_N(K)^\bullet),$$
using the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], where $Q$ is localization, $T_N(K)^i=N^{r_i}$, and the differential is $\gamma_{i+1}(1_N\otimes d_K^i)\gamma_i^{-1}$. Here $\gamma_i:N\otimes_B K^i\xrightarrow{1\otimes\theta_i}N\otimes_B B^{r_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}N^{r_i}$ uses the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with last map $z\otimes(b_j)\mapsto(b_jz)_j$ and inverse $(z_j)\mapsto\sum_jz_j\otimes e_j$. Thus, if $\theta_{i+1}d_K^i\theta_i^{-1}$ is locally the matrix $(a^i_{kj})$, the differential of $T_N(K)$ is $(z_j)\mapsto(\sum_j a^i_{kj}z_j)_k$. The comparison is induced by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the signed interchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on degrees $(p,q)$ of resolving complexes. In particular two-term and degree-zero finite free resolutions give respectively the complexes $[N^{r_{-1}}\to N^{r_0}]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ and $N^{r_0}[0]$, with these same transported differentials. No flatness of $N$ or existence of points of the site is assumed. If $0\to B^m\xrightarrow{f}B^n\xrightarrow{g}M\to0$ is a specified short exact sequence of $B$-module sheaves, then the augmentation $[B^m\xrightarrow{f}B^n]\to M[0]$ with degree-zero component $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so the preceding tensor formula applies to that very complex and its differential. Likewise a specified isomorphism $B^r\to M$ supplies the degree-zero quasi-isomorphism augmentation $B^r[0]\to M[0]$.

source.place: Tags 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); blueprint main-20261015, det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc proof, Local models, finite free complex and its tensor with any N

proof.text: For any $B$-module sheaf $F$ and finite $r$, define $c_{F,r}:F\otimes_B B^r\to F^r$ by $z\otimes(b_j)\mapsto(b_jz)_j$. This is balanced on sections and commutes with restrictions. The sheafification universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied to [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], gives the sheaf map. Its inverse is $(z_j)\mapsto\sum_j z_j\otimes e_j$, using the sheafification-unit images of these tensors. The composites are the identity: one gives $(z_j)$, while the other gives $\sum_j b_jz\otimes e_j=z\otimes\sum_j b_je_j=z\otimes(b_j)$. These identities on the presheaf tensor imply the identity after sheafification by its universal property. All maps are natural in $F$, including $r=0$, when both objects are zero. Composing with $1_F\otimes\theta_i$ gives the specified $\gamma_i$ when $F=N$.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), tensor as sheafified sectionwise tensor; coordinate verification

proof.text: In the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], taking $r$ copies preserves kernels and cokernels: a map into a finite product is uniquely its coordinate maps, so the kernel is the product of the kernels; dually, maps out of the finite biproduct identify its cokernel with the biproduct of the cokernels. Thus it preserves images and short exact sequences. Step 1 naturally identifies $F\mapsto F\otimes_B K^i$ with $F\mapsto F^{r_i}$. Consequently this tensor functor is exact, which is precisely the flatness of $K^i$ in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. This argument is in the abelian category, without asserting surjectivity on sections of an arbitrary sheaf epimorphism.

source.place: Definition 03ER (definition-flat), sheaf flatness; elementary finite-biproduct argument

proof.text: The complex $K$ is zero above $b$ by hypothesis and all its terms are flat by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] to $(\mathcal C,B,K,b)$ to obtain K-flatness for the direct-sum total tensor. The site's objects and arrows are sets by the site convention in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; use a common containing coefficient universe, as in the module-sheaf and derived-category conventions. This supplies the required essential smallness and requires no points of the site.

The ordinary symmetry of sheaf tensor is induced by $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$ by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For any two complexes $P,L$, define $\sigma:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B L)\to\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_B P)$ on the $(p,q)$ summand by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$. With the total differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $\sigma d$ has coefficients $(-1)^{(p+1)q}=(-1)^{pq+q}$ on $y\otimes d_Px$ and $(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$ on $d_Ly\otimes x$; these are the coefficients in $d\sigma$. Hence this is a cochain map. Interchanging again gives the sign $(-1)^{pq+qp}=1$, so it is an isomorphism. The formulas commute with restrictions and cochain maps, and induce maps on the direct sum since each summand goes to one summand. In particular for $L=N[0]$ all interchange signs are $1$.

source.place: Following Definition 06YU (definition-derived-tor), canonical symmetry; explicit total-complex sign check

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], the K-flat complex $K$ with flat terms has a canonical comparison $Q\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_B N[0])\cong QK\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QN[0]$, with no condition on $N$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q\epsilon:QK\to M[0]$ is invertible. Compose $(Q\epsilon\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}1)^{-1}$, the inverse of this comparison, and $Q\sigma$ from step 4. This gives $M[0]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N[0]\cong Q\operatorname{Tot}(N[0]\otimes_B K)$. Thus the comparison uses the given augmentation, the actual total tensor, and its signed interchange. On resolving complexes that interchange is precisely the map of step 4; its naturality makes it compatible with the inverted quasi-isomorphisms in the fixed-tensor descent statement. No flatness of $N$ is used.

source.place: Tags 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor), one-sided K-flat computation and localization

proof.text: In $\operatorname{Tot}(N[0]\otimes_B K)$ the only nonzero summand of total degree $i$ has bidegree $(0,i)$. Its term is $N\otimes_B K^i$ and its differential is $1_N\otimes d_K^i$, since $d_{N[0]}=0$ and $(-1)^0=1$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Transport through $\gamma_i$ of step 1: the differential becomes $\delta_i=\gamma_{i+1}(1_N\otimes d_K^i)\gamma_i^{-1}$, and $\delta_{i+1}\delta_i=\gamma_{i+2}(1_N\otimes(d_K^{i+1}d_K^i))\gamma_i^{-1}=0$. Hence the $\gamma_i$ are a cochain isomorphism onto $T_N(K)$. If the transported differential of $K$ has matrix $(a^i_{kj})$ on an object of the site, it sends $e_j$ to $\sum_k a^i_{kj}e_k$. Applying $1_N\otimes d$ to $\sum_j z_j\otimes e_j$ and then $\gamma_{i+1}$ gives $\bigl(\sum_j a^i_{kj}z_j\bigr)_k$. This formula respects restriction, so also applies to locally specified matrices. Composing its localization with step 5 proves the stated isomorphism and the asserted differential.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), balanced tensor relations; total differential as in homology Definition 012Z

proof.text: For a specified exact sequence $0\to B^m\xrightarrow fB^n\xrightarrow gM\to0$, put $K^{-1}=B^m$, $K^0=B^n$, $d^{-1}=f$, all other terms zero, and $\epsilon^0=g$. Since $gf=0$ this is a cochain augmentation. Its cohomology is $H^{-1}K=\ker f=0$, $H^0K=\operatorname{coker}f\cong M$ via $g$, and zero in all other degrees. The last isomorphism follows from exactness: $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$ and $g$ is an epimorphism in the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. A specified isomorphism $B^r\to M$ likewise gives a cochain isomorphism in degree zero. Steps 1–6 apply to these very complexes, with identity coordinate trivializations and ranks zero outside $[-1,0]$ or $\{0\}$, giving the two displayed special cases and their actual transported differentials. The cohomology formula used here is that of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

from.place: Local models: a complex of finite free modules is K-flat and its derived tensor with any N is the same matrix on finite powers of N, including length zero

split_report.summary: Kept the complete statement. Reused existing site bounded-flat K-flat and fixed-K-flat tensor descent tools; wrote out finite-coordinate inverses, exactness of finite powers, signed interchange, transported matrix differential and the two augmentation checks. No new nodes. All cited statements were read and quotes recorded.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Local models paragraph of det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc: the supplied finite free complex is flat and K-flat, its tensor with any N is the same matrix on finite powers, and length-one/zero augmentations give the indicated degree ranges. No change to unit or chapter route.

tool_uses.why: General ringed-site bounded-above-flat criterion, applied after proving finite free terms flat; the localizing-closure unit supplies no such general criterion.
Only the ordinary symmetry of sheaf tensor induced by module symmetry is used; the signed cochain formula is checked here. This is a generic structural tool, not a replacement of the unit route.

General one-sided K-flat computation of the existing site derived tensor with an arbitrary other complex; needed because the statement of two-resolving-object tensor descent alone does not compute with nonflat N.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-116d0237e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all 7 steps. The delivery adds no new nodes, and there is no repair or re-split note for this item. I checked every cited statement. Step 1: the coordinate isomorphism follows from sectionwise finite products and the sheafification universal property. Step 2: flatness follows because a finite biproduct is exact. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat applies (it is Stacks 06YQ, sites-cohomology.tex:3120), and the site convention gives the smallness it needs. Step 4: I recomputed both signs of the signed interchange. Step 5: lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated gives the one-sided K-flat comparison without any flatness of N, and Qε is invertible. Step 6: the matrix formula (z_j)↦(Σ_j a_kj z_j)_k is verified on generators. Step 7: the augmentations give H^{-1}=ker f=0 and H^0=coker f≅M via g. This matches the blueprint main-20261015 Local models paragraph (ctf-equals-bc proof, lines 8-16) and the parent lem-sfb-scalar-model-finite-flat-resolution's two citations. Edge cases checked: N=0, zero ranks, and the nonflat Z/2 example, which gives [Z/2 -0-> Z/2]. There is no cycle in the 142-node closure. No SGA source is used. Duplicate candidates were checked and differ: lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars, lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-tensor-complex, lem-weil-pbc-site-tensor-local-model-comparison and lem-trf-finite-filtered-flat-resolution. All three declared tool uses are generic and accepted.
